newsitem.title: FRANCE: France seeks details on Boeing-McDonnell pact.
newsitem.headline: France seeks details on Boeing-McDonnell pact.

text.p: Prime Minister Lionel Jospin said on Friday that France was reserving judgment on Boeing Co's planned merger with McDonnell Douglas, saying Paris needed more details of the $15 billion tie-up.
Jospin also told Radio Luxembourg the European Commission may have been too quick in signalling approval in principle to the merger on Wednesday, hoping to avoid a transatlantic trade war.

Asked if the U.S. giant had made enough concessions, Jospin said: "That needs to be examined. I think it's both the measure of the concessions and their effective implementation by Boeing-McDonnell Douglas that should really allow us to judge."
"Boeing's aeronautical position was already dominant. This merger...naturally poses problems," he said.

"We're not going to accept that the Commission sets rules in Europe to avoid dominant positions and virtual monopolies for European companies and then give approval for a very large American company," he said.

Boeing has agreed not to conclude any new exclusive aircraft supply contracts with airlines before August 1, 2007. It also agreed not to enforce the exclusivity provisions in its existing contracts with AMR Corp's American Airlines, Continental Airlines and Delta Airlines.
A final Commision decision on the merger is expected next week after a review by EU national anti-trust experts.

Asked if the Commission had signalled approval too quickly, Jospin said: "Perhaps. We want to know what is the exact impact of the European commitments before giving our position as French government."
